Who eligible to apply for Palo Alto home electrification rebates?
Palo Alto residents with active electric and gas utility services; you will need your utility account number to apply. If you are a property owner without an account number associated with your Palo Alto property, use either your tenant’s account number or contact us at utilityprograms@paloalto.gov for assistance. If you rent your home, encourage your landlord to switch to electric.
Is there a cut-off date for when projects needed to be completed to qualify for a rebate?
All rebate applications must be submitted no later than 90 days after the project has passed final inspection. The Induction Cooktop/Range and Portable Induction Cooktop rebates are only available for projects completed on or after March 18, 2026.
Can I apply for add-on rebates, such as insulation or electrical panel upgrades, separately?
No, add-on rebates are only available in combination with heat pump water heater (HPWH), heat pump HVAC, or Induction Cooktop/Range rebates.
If I plan to install a combined space heating and water heating system, can I apply for both the HPWH rebate and HP HVAC rebate?
Yes, a combined heat pump system qualifies for both HPWH and HP HVAC rebates. However, you must apply for each rebate separately.
What is a CPAU Instant Rebate Partner, and what are the benefits of selecting them?
Selecting a CPAU Instant Rebate Partner lets you take advantage of instant savings and a hassle-free rebate process.
Immediate Discount – Receive your entire CPAU rebate at the point of sale, reducing your upfront costs.
Hassle-free Process – Your contractor manages and submits the rebate application on your behalf.

To find a CPAU Instant Rebate partner, check the Contractor Directory in the Rebate Hub and look for the City of Palo Alto Instant Rebate banner on the contractor’s tile.
How long will it take to receive approval after submitting my rebate reservation?
The City will typically review and approve rebate reservations within 5 business days. If additional information is required, you will receive an email notification with next steps.
How long will it take to receive my rebate after submitting the final application?
Once your final rebate application is approved, the rebate payment will be processed and sent via check within approximately five weeks. Ensure all required documentation is submitted to avoid delays.
Why do I need to submit a W-9 for the gas meter removal incentive?
The City of Palo Alto considers gas meter disconnection incentives to be taxable income and will not disburse any incentive without having first received a W-9 form from the Customer. By submitting these tax forms, Participants agree that they are responsible for consulting their own tax advisor as to the tax consequences associated with all incentives and rebates provided by the City of Palo Alto. Personal information provided on the W-9 will be used by the City of Palo for tax reporting purposes only.

url: https://1800coolaid.com/hvac-rebates-california-2026/

If you read an HVAC rebate article written before 2026, most of it is now wrong. Three of the four programs that used to stack on a Bay Area heat pump installation have closed, and the utility rebates people remember from PG&E are no longer on PG&E's list. What is left is smaller, more local and more rule-bound, but it is real money if you plan for it.
This page is our running status check on every program a California homeowner is likely to hear about, written from the programs' own pages rather than from other contractors' blogs. For the full winter heating picture, including the Bay Area's new rules on gas furnaces, see our Winter Heating Help Center.
What has closed
ProgramStatus in 2026
Federal 25C tax credit (heat pumps, furnaces, AC)Ended for equipment placed in service after 31 December 2025 (IRS). A system installed in 2025 or earlier is still claimed on that year's return.
TECH Clean California (single-family heat pump HVAC)Fully reserved since 14 November 2025; not accepting new reservations (TECH Clean California).
HEEHRA (the state's federally funded home electrification rebates)Single-family rebates fully reserved statewide; waitlist only (California Energy Commission).
California Energy-Smart Homes2026 incentive funding fully subscribed as of April 2026 (BayREN).
BayREN Home+ heat pump rebateNo longer available as of April 2024 (BayREN).
PG&E residential HVAC rebatesNone listed. PG&E's residential rebates page currently lists a generator and battery rebate, a used EV rebate and an EV charging rebate, but no heat pump, AC, furnace or thermostat rebates (PG&E).

If you see any of these quoted as available for a 2026 installation, including in an online cost calculator, treat the whole estimate with suspicion.
What is still open: local electricity providers
Most of the Bay Area buys its electricity through a community choice provider or a city utility, even though PG&E still delivers it and sends the bill. Those local providers now fund most of the heat pump rebates. Which one you have depends on your address, and the provider's name is printed on your PG&E bill.

args.html:
HOME HVAC · PALO ALTO, CA

Choose the heat pump

For an 1,800 sq ft Palo Alto house, a heat pump is the better long-term pick. The city rebate narrows the upfront gap, and you get cooling in the same unit.

Heat pump, unless your furnace is fine. Palo Alto's mild climate suits heat pumps well. Palo Alto Utilities offers up to $2,500 (up to $5,000 if income-eligible), and the federal credit is gone, so don't count on it. Apply for the rebate before you install.
$3.5–7.5kGas furnace installed
$5–12kHeat pump installed (one source; others quote higher for full ducted variable-speed systems)
$2,500CPAU rebate (up to $5k income-qualified)
$0Federal 25C credit (ended 12/31/2025)

Part 1

Costs

Gas furnaceHeat pump
Installed cost (1800coolaid.com)$3,500–$7,500$5,000–$12,000
Higher-end quote (havencostguide.com)Central AC $7k–$14k (a furnace alone costs less)$12k–$22k for variable-speed ducted
Cooling includedNo, you need separate ACYes
Rebate availableNone found in Bay AreaUp to $2,500 (CPAU)

Running costs: one 2026 California guide finds a heat pump and gas furnace cost about the same to run at standard PG&E rates. The heat pump pulls ahead on a time-of-use or electrification rate, or with solar. Caveat: Palo Alto buys from the city utility (CPAU), not PG&E, so its gas and electric rates differ. Check your own bill and run the numbers on CPAU's current rates before deciding.

Part 2

Efficiency

Gas furnaceHeat pump
Typical efficiency (general industry figures, not from sources above)80–98% AFUE, so at most 1 unit of heat per unit of fuelRoughly 200–400% (COP 2–4) in mild weather, because it moves heat rather than making it
On-site emissionsCombustion, with CO risk if a heat exchanger failsNone
Cold-weather performanceUnaffectedEfficiency dips below freezing, which rarely matters in Palo Alto

Part 3

Incentives (checked in 2026)

  • Palo Alto Utilities: up to $2,500 for a heat pump replacing a gas heater, up to $5,000 if income-eligible. Add-on rebates for insulation or panel upgrades are available only with a heat pump rebate.
  • Instant rebate partners: a contractor with the City of Palo Alto Instant Rebate banner takes the rebate off at the point of sale and files the paperwork.
  • Combined systems: a combined space and water heat pump can claim both the HVAC and water heater rebates, applied for separately.
  • Federal 25C credit ended for equipment placed in service after 12/31/2025.
  • TECH Clean California and HEEHRA are fully reserved, with waitlist only.
  • PG&E lists no heat pump or furnace rebates.
  • Rebate deadline: apply within 90 days of final inspection. Programs often need pre-approval, so don't replace in a rush.

Part 4

Which to choose

Pick a heat pump if

  • You want AC too, or need to replace both
  • You have or plan solar
  • Your furnace is near end of life
  • You want the city rebate

Keep or replace with gas if

  • Your furnace works and is under about 15 years old
  • Your panel needs an expensive upgrade
  • Your ducts are poor and the budget is tight

Next

Steps

  1. Check your CPAU gas and electric rates and your electric panel capacity.
  2. Get 2–3 quotes from CPAU Instant Rebate partner contractors, including a Manual J load calculation and duct check.
  3. Reserve the rebate before signing or installing.
  4. Install with a permit, then submit final paperwork within 90 days of inspection.
Prices are ranges from contractor-written guides, not firm quotes. Rebate amounts change, so confirm on the city page.
